title: Heat Pumps in 2026 | What you should know
summary: A Denver HVAC contractor explains heat pump types, dual fuel versus air handler setups, new refrigerants, early-2025 tax credits and why the installer matters more than the brand.

assertions.quote: There are lots of heat pumps that maintain 100% capacity all the way below 0° Fahrenheit before they start to lose capacity
But the bottom line is this is just a myth.
often times you will find yourself opting for a dual fuel system just for both comfort and efficiency sake because they are more efficient.
right now on all Airsource heat pumps, which are traditional style heat pumps, there is a $2,000 tax credit that is federal.
a geothermal heat pump qualifies for up to a 30% tax credit of the total purchase price.

verdicts.note: The 25D residential clean energy credit covered 30% of ground-source heat pump costs without a dollar cap until it ended after 2025.

assertions.quote: the state of Colorado has a $1,500 tax credit also available for anyone that installs a heat pump.

verdicts.note: Some states and utilities pay thousands of dollars, but programs vary widely and many areas offer little.

assertions.quote: The bottom line is that brand, in my opinion, is not as important

verdicts.note: Installation and sizing faults affect performance more than brand differences among major manufacturers, but evidence is mostly practitioner consensus.
Lower-than-expected COPs were not consistently from certain manufacturers, while sizing explained the high auxiliary use; brand and sizing are not compared head to head.

assertions.quote: that can be the difference between a system working well, troublefree for years, or you having repeated issues and repeated service calls
Inverter-driven systems are number one most efficient. Number two, they're most quiet.

verdicts.note: Variable-speed compressors have higher SEER2/HSPF2 ratings and lower sound levels at part load.

assertions.quote: if you have a 410A system, not to worry. You don't have to rush out and replace it right away.

verdicts.note: The AIM Act phase-down limits new equipment production; existing systems can still be serviced with R-410A.

EPA's HFC restrictions set GWP limits on newly manufactured systems for new construction and major retrofits (with installs of pre-2025 equipment allowed until 2026); they do not reach existing working systems.

assertions.quote: typically this is going to be more cost-effective because you don't have to have an added furnace and evaporator coil

verdicts.note: An air handler is usually cheaper than a furnace plus coil, but a dual-fuel retrofit that keeps a working furnace can cost less.
